production_calls.observation: captureSession() reads the suffix after a per-Session handoff cursor, optionally stops at inclusive throughSeq, redacts and emits each event in sequence order, and advances the cursor only after emit returns.

All-history input scans events in order and retains eligible nonempty human text messages only through the generation watermark. Automatic first-prompt work instead uses the titleInput projection. Explicit refresh uses all-history input for either cadence.

Pre-commit title validation requires unique earlier seqs naming any human-sourced user/message, including blank and non-text messages. It rejects other event types and plugin-sourced messages before publication.
Invariant installation scans already-live Sessions; newly created Sessions use the exact SessionCreationBaseline from A14. This bootstrap scan remains a separate retained history read.

current_read_count.expected_after_A17: Two source occurrences remain: S071 and the existing-session bootstrap scan.

dependency_direction.observed: session-query imports and peer-depends on session-title; session-title does not depend on session-query.
dependency_direction.cycle_rule: Do not add session-query to session-title.

focused_verification.command: git diff --check -- packages/core/session packages/session/session-telemetry packages/session/session-title packages/session-query/session-query .agent

findings: S071 remains unchanged because session-query observations copy a full fixed prefix and cannot preserve suffix handoff timing or cursor behavior.
S072 must load history through a mandatory provider method; first-prompt automatic input stays projection-owned while all-history and explicit refresh use the provider loader.
S073 must index all earlier human user/message events, including blank and non-text messages, and only update from committed event objects.

After awaiting a provider loader, SessionTitleService must call assertCurrent(session, work) before invoking generate; cancellation, failure, disposal, session removal, and service teardown need regressions.

decision.problem: Remove the remaining Session-title consumer reads from deprecated synchronous APIs while preserving telemetry handoff and the title invariant's synchronous veto.
invariants: Telemetry keeps its current synchronous per-event redaction and handoff semantics until a bounded live suffix reader exists.
Title provider input contains the complete eligible ordered human-text prefix through its captured inclusive watermark, including fork-inherited history, with no later prompt.
Explicit refresh still uses all eligible messages even when automatic cadence is first-prompt; automatic first-prompt work continues to use titleInput projection state.
An aborted or superseded history load cannot invoke generation or append a title; the service rechecks its current work immediately after the asynchronous load.
A title citation names an earlier, unique, human-sourced user/message event; the check remains synchronous and can veto before publication.
No released Session data, SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION, persistence schema, or wire payload changes.

candidates.reason: It preserves the exact handoff cursor, inclusive cut, redaction timing, ordered per-event acceptance, and cursor-after-emit behavior.
The existing observation materializes a full prefix and adds an asynchronous read/emit window; it cannot preserve bounded suffix work, detached snapshot capture, and current cursor semantics.
session-query already depends on session-title, so this direction creates a package cycle.

A mandatory SessionTitleProvider.loadMessages({session, throughSeq, signal}) keeps query ownership in the provider layer, uses the existing session-query fixed-cut observation, and leaves title core dependent on no query package.
It performs one deprecated history lookup per citation even though a local committed-message index can preserve the exact predicate at the synchronous dispatch hook.
An asynchronous lookup cannot veto the already synchronous Session.append operation.

A WeakMap keyed by Session stores all human user/message seqs, seeds from existing-session scans and SessionCreationBaseline, and updates after session/event only when isCommittedEvent accepts the exact event.

provider_input_contract.semantics: Return every eligible nonempty human text message in seq order through inclusive throughSeq. The title service validates the exact returned snapshot and supplies it unchanged to generate.
call_sites: Explicit refresh for both first-prompt and all-prompts providers
provider_input_contract.first_prompt: Automatic first-prompt work continues to use the existing titleInput projection and does not call loadMessages.
provider_input_contract.query_read: The shared title-LLM provider helper retains a sessionQuery observation lease only while mapping its captured events, filters events to throughSeq, and then disposes the lease.
provider_input_contract.ordering: ensureFallback remains before message loading; after await loadMessages, the service calls assertCurrent before generate, then keeps the existing post-generate current-work check and result validation.
provider_input_contract.failure: A rejected load follows the current provider failure path; it cannot invoke generate or append a provider title. Automatic logging and explicit-refresh rejection remain service-owned.

citation_index.contents: Every committed human-sourced user/message seq, including blank and non-text messages; do not reuse the narrower title-input eligibility filter.
citation_index.seed: Existing-live Session event scan and SessionCreationBaseline.events for new Sessions.
citation_index.update: Global session/event listener adds only a human user/message event for which session.isCommittedEvent(event) is true.
citation_index.validation: Preserve unique, valid SessionSeq and strict seq < title-event.seq checks, then test index membership inside internal/dispatch before publication.
citation_index.lifetime: WeakMap permits Session collection; one numeric seq is retained per human user/message for the live Session lifetime.

invalid_cases: Appending a prompt after the title watermark while a load is delayed must not place it in provider input.
Superseding or disposing a provider during load must abort/cancel the read and must not invoke generate or append a title.
A loader rejection must skip generate and preserve the already accepted fallback title.
Missing sessionQuery must fail provider plugin loading rather than silently falling back to snapshotEvents.
A fake user/message session/event emission for a seq owned by a non-message event must not poison the citation index.
Plugin-sourced messages, other event kinds, current/future seqs, duplicates, and malformed citation seqs must still be rejected before commit.
A citation to an earlier human user/message with blank or non-text content must remain accepted, matching the current invariant.

documentation_and_compatibility.public_api: Update SessionTitleProvider and every package/test consumer because public APIs are pre-stable.
documentation_and_compatibility.composition: Both shipped provider plugins declare and inject sessionQuery; the base bundle already supplies session-query-sqlite. Missing service is a load-time error.
documentation_and_compatibility.docs: Update English and Chinese package READMEs, JSDoc, pairing records, package dependency manifests, and relevant generated module graph after M08 stabilizes.
documentation_and_compatibility.model_visibility: The eligible message array, request framing, message seqs, route, and logged session/title-llm-request remain byte-for-byte equivalent; no snapshot or SDK output change is expected unless regression evidence shows a transcript difference.

residual_risks: session-query observeSession materializes the full fixed prefix; S072 needs the complete message input, but the current API does not provide bounded event pages.

The citation index adds one retained sequence number per human user/message for each live Session; retain the WeakMap owner and validate this memory cost against real Session sizes before considering a core-wide index.
reopen_conditions: Revisit S071 when a lower-level reader can provide bounded ordered suffixes for live and detached cuts while preserving emit/redaction/cursor behavior.
Revisit S072 if a query API provides event pages over one fixed cut or the all-prompts provider contract changes with explicit model-input compatibility evidence.
Revisit S073 if the citation predicate or Session event ownership changes, or measured index memory justifies moving the index into core/session.
